title: Primary mouse osteoblast and osteoclast culturing and analysis
protocol: Prepare 12-well cell culture plate containing 1 mL basal medium per well (3 wells for each bone).
Prepare 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube for each collected bone, filled with 1 mL of basal medium.
Sacrifice 3-week-old male mice and immediately dip the whole body into 70% EtOH.
Bring the mouse to the primary cell culture hood and place it in a petri dish.
Extract the femurs, tibias, and humeri with sterile tools.
Remove skin, tendons, and muscles from bones using a sterile gauze.
Cut the epiphyses of bones to collect bone marrow into 1.5 mL tubes.
Maintain sterility throughout the procedure; ensure that the hood and materials are clean.
Remove any residue of muscle, tendons, or skin from the bones.
Place each cleaned bone in an individual well of a 12-well plate.
Cut the epiphyses of the bones with a small scissors.
Flush the bone marrow several times with a 1 mL syringe using a 25G needle in a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube containing 1 mL basal medium until the bone becomes devoid of bone marrow and turns white.
Place the flushed bone back into a clean well of the 12-well plate containing basal medium for osteoblast culture.
Collect the bone marrow-containing Eppendorf tubes for osteoclast culture.
Flush the bones at least four times with basal medium in the 12-well plate to remove other cells from the surface of the bone.
Move bone to a new clean well filled with basal medium and flush one last time.
Cut each bone into small pieces of 1 mm length using sterile scissors.
Place the cut bone pieces into a 25 cm² flask containing 6 ml digestion medium.
Incubate the flask for 90 min at 37°C with mild shaking in vertical position.
Aspirate the digestion medium from the flask, keeping only the bone pieces inside.
Rinse the flask twice with 10 ml basal medium and discard the medium each time.
Add 6 mL basal medium to the flask with bone pieces.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 3–4 days.
Check the flasks once to see if the cells have spread from the bone particles.
Change the medium after 3–4 days if the cells have not exceeded 70%–80% confluence.
Follow the passaging protocol once the cells reach 80% confluence.
Wait for each flask to reach 70%–80% confluence and passage them independently.
For the first passage, add 2 mL of collagenase I solution (1 mg/mL in 0.9% NaCl) to cover the surface of the flask.
Incubate at 37°C for 8 minutes.
Add 5 mL basal medium to stop the digestion and collect the medium completely in a 50 mL falcon tube.
To the 25 cm² flask, add 2 mL trypsin and incubate at 37°C for 3 minutes to detach remaining cells.
Check under the microscope to confirm most of the cells are well detached from the flask and add 5 mL basal medium to stop the process.
Flush the flask several times to detach the cells and collect the medium in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge the collected medium at 178 × g for 8 min at 4°C.
Use a 5 mL serological pipette with an enlarged aspirating end to collect remaining pieces of bones with basal medium.
Transfer all bone pieces and collected medium to a new 75 cm² flask.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant from the cells after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cells in 15 ml basal medium.
Transfer all cells to respective new 75 cm² flasks ensuring even spread of bone pieces.
Incubate the cells at 37°C until they reach 90% confluence.
Change the medium with basal medium every 3–4 days while cells grow.
Proceed with passage when cells reach 90% confluence using steps from protocol.
Prepare fresh collagenase solution from powder and pass through a 0.22 μm filter.
Incubate the flask containing cells in collagenase solution for 8 min at 37°C.
Add 10 ml basal medium to stop digestion and collect the medium in a 50 ml falcon tube.
Incubate the 75 cm² flask with 6 ml trypsin for 3 min at 37°C.
Check under microscope to confirm >90% cell detachment from flask.
Add 10 ml basal medium to stop digestion and collect cells in a 50 ml falcon tube.
Centrifuge the collected cells at 178 × g or 8 min at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant from the cells.
Resuspend the cells in 15 mL basal medium.
Count the cells.
Seed approximately 9 × 10^6 cells in 15 mL basal medium at a density of 6 × 10^5 cells/mL or 1.2 × 10^5 cells/cm² in a new 75 cm² culture flask for each of the original flasks.
Let the cells grow until they reach 90% confluence.
Change the medium with basal medium every 3–4 days.
Passage the cells again when they reach 90% confluence, repeating steps from the process.
Pool three T75 flasks once they have been passaged at least 3 times and reached between 70% to 90% confluence after being derived from three different animals.
Trash the flask immediately if bacterial, fungal, or mycoplasma contamination is detected.
Estimate the cell number needed for each experiment (quantitative PCR, ALP measurement, mineralization, collagen production) according to your experimental design and conditions.
Calculate the number of plates required in your experimental setup and prepare Osteoblast stimulation medium accordingly.
Wait until three T75 flasks reach approximately 90% confluence after being passaged at least three times.
Pool cells from the three T75 flasks into one 50-mL tube once all three flasks have reached 90% confluence.
Centrifuge the pooled cell mixture for 8 minutes at 178 × g and 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of basal medium.
Count live cells using Trypan blue.
Seed cells into plates in accordance with the specified concentrations: for a 6-well plate, use 1.4 × 10^5 cells/well in 2 mL medium; for a 12-well plate, use 7 × 10^4 cells/well in 1 mL medium.
Check cells every day until they reach 100% confluence.
Change the medium to osteoblast stimulation medium and add treatment of interest as soon as 100% confluence is reached.
Change the medium every 3-4 days with osteoblast stimulation medium and the added treatment.
Stop the experiment and perform RNA collection after 7 days for characterization of osteoblasts.
Flush the bone marrow from each bone in 1.5-mL Eppendorf tubes.
Resuspend the bone marrow by gently flushing up and down through a needle (25G) several times, avoiding bubbles.
Pool all the bone marrow from one mouse coming from tibia, femur, and humeri.
Pass the cells through a 70-μm filter to collect them in a 50-mL falcon tube.
Top up the volume of bone marrow in a 75 cm² flask with basal medium containing 10 ng/mL M-CFS (one flask per animal).
Incubate for 24 h at 37°C in a 5% CO₂ incubator.
Confirm there is no bacterial or fungal contamination by checking the medium coloration and cell growth.
Collect the supernatant that contains the cells not adhering to the flask.
Centrifuge cells collected from the 3 animals in a 50 mL tube (8 min at 178 × g-4°C).
Resuspend the centrifuged cells in 5 mL basal medium containing 30 ng/mL M-CFS.
Count the live cells using trypan blue.
Seed the cells in basal medium containing 30 ng/mL M-CFS.
Maintain the cell culture conditions for myeloid progenitors before differentiation medium is added.
Incubate the cells under early osteoclast differentiation conditions (2 to 4 days after differentiation medium is added).
Continue incubation for intermediary osteoclast differentiation, noting larger cells starting to become multinucleated (5 to 7 days post-differentiation medium addition).
Incubate further until full osteoclast differentiation is observed with numerous nuclei and large cell size (7 to 10 days after differentiation medium was added).
Monitor the culture for dead osteoclasts one day following full differentiation, noting burst cells indicated by arrows.
Seed 4 × 10^5 cells per well in a 6-well plate using 2 mL medium (2 × 10^5 cells/mL or 4.2 × 10^4 cells/cm²).
Seed 1 × 10^5 cells per well in a 12-well plate using 1 mL medium (2.6 × 10^4 cells/cm²).
After 48 hours, change the medium and initiate osteoclast differentiation.
Monitor cell differentiation daily during the process.
Change the osteoclast differentiation medium every 4 days.
Aspirate the medium from cells when they are at day 7 of differentiation.
Wash the cells with 2 mL cold PBS.
Aspirate the PBS and add 1 mL of Trizol onto the wells under a chemical hood.
Rinse cell cultures at day 7 of the protocol with 2 mL of sterile PBS under cell culture hood after aspirating the media.
Discard the PBS and scrape the cells in 0.5 mL Milli-Q H2O with a cell scraper.
Collect the 0.5 mL of scraped cells in water in Eppendorf tubes.
Sonicate the samples three times with 5 seconds of pausing at 30% duty cycle and output control as "2".
Adjust the amplitude of power by 20%.
Keep samples on ice to avoid heating and deterioration of proteins.
Centrifuge at 11292 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Prepare a reactive solution by mixing 1 mL of 100 mM p-NPP, 8 mL of 0.7 M 2-amino-2-methyl-1-propanol, 0.1 mL of 100 mM MgCl2, and 0.9 mL of Milli-Q Water.
Transfer 100 μL of the supernatant from the centrifuged sample to a 1.5 mL tube.
Take 200 μL of supernatant in a new collection tube and store at -20°C for later measurement of protein concentration.
Incubate the tubes at 37°C for 10 min.
Add 900 μL of warm reactive solution to the 100 μL warm samples (37°C) and start a timer.
Hydrolyze the solution by ALP until it turns yellow.
Stop the reaction by adding 200 μL of NaOH 1N when the solution is yellow.
Vortex samples briefly after stopping the reaction.
Transfer 200 μL from each tube into a 96-well plate for spectrophotometer reading.
Read the optical density (OD) at 405 nm with a spectrophotometer.
Rinse cell cultures with 2 mL of sterile PBS under cell culture hood.
Fix cells with 2 mL of 3.7% formaldehyde per well for 1–2 h at 15°C–25°C.
Discard formaldehyde and rinse with 2 mL of Milli-Q water per well.
Rinse cells with 2 mL of Milli-Q water per well.
Stain with 1 mL of 2% (w/v) Alizarin Red-S for a maximum of 1 h at 15°C–25°C under gentle agitation.
Wash the plate several times with Milli-Q water by filling the wells to the top and aspirating it.
Let the plates dry under the hood or gently tap the plate to dry it on tissue paper.
Use cotton swabs to clean dye remnants from the sides of the plate.
Take pictures of the cells under the microscope for illustration or identification of calcification regions.
Destain the cells with 2 mL of 10% (w/v) hexadecyl pyridinium chloride for 1 h at 15°C–25°C under gentle agitation.
Pre-heat the solution to dissolve precipitates.
Collect 200 μL of each well in the 96-well plate.
Measure the absorbance at 550 nm with a spectrophotometer.
Add 200 μL hexadecyl pyridinium chloride as a blank control.
Dilute sample solution with hexadecyl pyridinium chloride if sample absorption is greater than 1.2 value.
Estimate Alizarin Red staining using the formula: Alizarin red staining (AU) = Abs sample – Abs blank.
Where Abs sample = Optical density of the sample measured at 550 nm.
Where Abs blank = Optical density of the blank measured at 550 nm.
Normalize results with the control group.
Rinse cell cultures with 2 mL of sterile PBS under cell culture hood after aspirating the media.
Fix cells with 2 mL of 3.7% formaldehyde per well for 1–2 h at 15°C–25°C.
Discard formaldehyde and rinse with 2 mL of Milli-Q water per well.
Wash the plate 3 times with deionized water.
Dry the culture plates at 15°C–25°C.
Add 1 mL of Sirius red dye reagent per well for 1 h with low shaking at 15°C–25°C.
Wash extensively with 0.01 N HCl to remove all unbound dye and aspirate the solution.
Remove the excess wash solution and let the plates dry under the hood, or gently tap the plate to a tissue paper to dry.
Take pictures of the cells under the microscope.
Dissolve Sirius red dye by adding 0.2 mL of 0.1 N sodium hydroxide and shaking for 30 minutes at 15°C–25°C.
Collect 200 μL from each well in a 96-well plate.
Measure the absorbance at 550 nm with a spectrophotometer.
Add 200 μL of sodium hydroxide solution as a blank control.
Dilute sample solutions with sodium hydroxide if sample absorption is greater than 1.2.
Normalize the results with the control group.
Prepare staining solutions fresh every time for TRAP Staining.
Dissolve Fast violet B dye and let it agitate for 30 min.
Filter the Fast violet B solution through a 45-μm filter in excess of filtering volume.
Store Fast violet B powder at 4°C and naphthol powder at -20°C.
Mix fast violet solution and naphthol solution at a 1:1 ratio in a small beaker simultaneously.
Agitate the mixed solutions with a magnetic stirrer for approximately 1 min.
Add 500 μl of solution per well.
Incubate for 14–16 hours at 4°C.
Discard the solution and wash with 2 mL water.
Add 500 μl of sodium fluoride solution and incubate for 30 minutes at 15°C–25°C.
Discard the solution and add 2 mL of water.
Proceed with imaging of the plate.
Count TRAP-positive cells (osteoclasts) by counting multinucleated, violet stained cells.
